description: This bar chart illustrates the Mean Average Precision at 10 (MAP@10) values for two different sampling strategies—labeled in the legend as “Uniform Sampling Strategy” (represented by purple bars) and “Uniform Sampling Strategy” (represented by yellow bars)—across varying values of m, which ranges from 6 to 10 along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, labeled “MAP@10,” is scaled linearly from 23.0 to 27.0, with tick marks spaced at 0.5-unit intervals. The chart is divided into two distinct groups of bars: the left group corresponds to m values 6 through 10, and the right group corresponds to m values 6 through 10. For each m value, there is one purple bar and one yellow bar, positioned side-by-side. The purple bars, representing the first strategy, are consistently taller than the yellow bars for the same m value, indicating higher MAP@10 scores. Specifically, the purple bars for m=6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 have approximate MAP@10 values of 26.0, 26.7, 26.3, 26.6, and 26.5, respectively. The yellow bars for the same m values have approximate MAP@10 values of 24.4, 24.8, 25.6, 25.3, and 24.4, respectively. The bars are not sorted by height; instead, they are arranged in ascending order of m along the horizontal axis. There is no visual emphasis such as shading, bolding, or outlining applied to any specific bar.
